decisions.reason: The candidate already has a message-154 MODIFY capturing the clarified requirement that E and L belong to the Hero-V-defined proprietary alphabet. The preservation Event adds that construction to the locked-assets list but does not require another candidate-state change.
The É accent's literal derivation and alignment were already locked before message 154, and the source Event does not change those rules.

The candidate already has a message-154 MODIFY expanding the Hero V's identity role to define the entire architectural vocabulary. Its approved geometry was already locked and is not newly changed by the preservation Event.
The source Event newly locks the E and L construction, not the second V's construction or right-arm character. Those second-V rules remain valid unchanged.
The candidate already has a message-154 MODIFY capturing the slight elevation and restrained-echo clarification. Its existing below-Hero-V-and-accent relationship remains unchanged.
The peak-alignment rule was already established and locked before message 154. Neither the source Event nor its new E-and-L locked asset changes that alignment.
Locking the architectural E and L construction has no necessary effect on accepted review-image delivery formats.
Message 154 does not change the wordmark's spacing or cohesive-reading requirement, and locking the E and L construction does not logically determine a new kerning rule.
The all-caps case treatment remains valid unchanged; the source decision concerns architectural vocabulary and preservation of design assets.
The source decision does not resume, alter, or otherwise affect the deferred champagne-gold material treatment.
Adding the E and L construction to the locked design assets does not change the final production-ready artwork handoff requirement.
